title: vendor rke2 CNI plugins + offline upgrade/rollback hooks for air-gapped installs
author: Leah Park
description: Motivation: Customers running Redwood Private on-prem with RKE2 often operate fully air-gapped clusters and require a bundled, validated CNI set plus deterministic upgrade/rollback behavior during offline upgrades. This PR vendors a minimal set of RKE2-compatible CNI artifacts (canal/flannel + calico dataplane bits and rke2-cni shim) into the offline bundle, adds a small SELinux module and policy packaging step required for RHEL environments, and introduces an idempotent offline upgrade/rollback hook framework so operators can perform safe rollbacks without internet access. What changed (high-level): 1) Packaging: added vendor/cni/ directory with compressed tarballs for canal and calico dataplane, rke2-cni shim, and SHA256 checksums. 2) Installer runtime: extend airgap preflight to verify CNI artifact signatures and space checks, and to unpack only the CNI payload needed by the target kube-distro. 3) Hooks: new hooks/upgrade-preflight.sh, hooks/upgrade-postinstall.sh, hooks/rollback.sh that run entirely offline; hooks implement graceful drain/uncordon, KV cache preservation for Redwood services, and automated iptables/ebtables cleanup. 4) SELinux: small rpm-style policy bundle and a conditional module loader used only on RHEL/OL family hosts. 5) Helm and manifests: a patched charts/redwood-system chart to allow using local image/asset references for CNI DaemonSet and to expose a cni.install.strategy value (bundle|host). 6) Tests & docs: integration test harness updates and an ops-guide section documenting offline upgrade/rollback commands and failure modes. Commits summary: - add vendor/cni payloads and checksums - implement offline preflight and unpack logic - add selinux module packaging and loader - add offline hook framework and idempotent rollback script - patch helm chart to accept local cni references - add integration tests and docs Notes and rationale: - We picked canal (flannel+calico) and a trimmed calico dataplane set because they cover the networking/mtu/ipam modes used by most customers and keep the vendor bundle size reasonable. - The rollback hook is intentionally conservative: it first attempts a fast rollback using Helm release history where available, then falls back to manual manifest restore using a timestamped snapshot kept in /var/lib/redwood/installer/snapshots. - SELinux module is optional at runtime; installer will skip and emit a warning on distros that don't support semodule. Files changed (high-level): - vendor/cni/canal-1.14.0.tar.gz.sha256 - vendor/cni/canal-1.14.0.tar.gz - vendor/cni/calico-dataplane-3.25.0.tar.gz - installer/preflight/checks_cni.go (new checks) - installer/runtime/unpack_airgap.go (unpack selector changes) - hooks/upgrade-preflight.sh - hooks/upgrade-postinstall.sh - hooks/rollback.sh - packaging/selinux/redwood_cni.pp - charts/redwood-system/values.yaml (cni.install.strategy) - charts/redwood-system/templates/cni-daemonset.yaml (local image refs) - integration/tests/airgap_cni_upgrade_test.sh - docs/ops/offline-upgrades.md Testing performed: - Local RKE2 clusters (v1.25 and v1.26) in air-gapped VM lab: full upgrade flow (install → upgrade → rollback) exercised end-to-end on Ubuntu 22.04 and RHEL 9. - SELinux module load/unload tested on RHEL 9.1. - CI: unit tests + integration script run in a simulated airgap (--local-bundle flag). Observed CI was flaky initially due to checksum handling; fixed by switching to streaming SHA256 verification and re-running pipelines. Security considerations: - All vendored artifacts are accompanied by SHA256 checksums and an internal GPG signature (keys stored in the private installer signing keyset). The installer enforces signature verification by default for air-gapped installs; operators can pass --insecure for lab usage. - The SELinux policy is minimal and scoped to the installer and CNI sockets; no broad permissions granted. Upgrade/rollback operator steps (short): 1) Place offline bundle on installer host and run ./install.sh --bundle /path/to/bundle --kube-distro rke2 2) To upgrade: ./installerctl upgrade --bundle /t/bundle --hooks enable 3) To rollback: ./installerctl rollback --to-snapshot 2025-11-18--21:04 4) If automatic rollback fails, manual restore path documented in docs/ops/offline-upgrades.md Related Linear/Jira: ENG-7421 (airgap CNI vendoring), ENG-7530 (rollback hooks), PM-1182 (ops guide). Release notes: - Air-gapped installs: vendor canal+calico dataplane for RKE2; verify artifacts offline - Installer will now expose cni.install.strategy and honor local CNI references for air-gapped clusters - Add offline upgrade/rollback hooks for safer on-prem upgrades - SELinux module packaging for RHEL-based hosts Known limitations: - Bundle size increases by ~120MB. We plan to move to delta artifact delivery in a follow-up (ENG-7689). - Currently validated for RKE2 and kubeadm; K3s support requires a follow-up patch to handle k3s-specific CNI shims. Merge and rollout: Squash-merged to main after approvals from Arman and Priya and passing CI. Backported docs and a brief ops note were included in the release checklist.

review_comments: Arman Singh: Left a couple of suggestions on the unpack selector — prefer explicit distro detection vs heuristic. Also flagged an edge case around partial unpack on low-disk nodes.
Leah Park: Addressed Arman's unpack selector comments; added a disk-space preflight and a stream-verify step to avoid partial unpacked artifacts.
Priya Natarajan: Approved after SELinux module scope trimmed and docs updated to call out the optional flag.
Samir Patel: CI flaky on first run due to checksum streaming; re-run fixed and I validated integration test logs.
release_notes: Vendor canal+calico CNI artifacts in the offline bundle for RKE2 air-gapped installs.
Add offline upgrade and rollback hooks to the installer; safe rollback uses Helm history or snapshot restore.
Introduce optional SELinux module packaging for RHEL hosts to avoid runtime denials.
Expose charts.redwood-system.cni.install.strategy to select bundle vs host install behavior.
